mainTopic: Bidding to redeem a שדה אחוזה from הקדש: the owner's חומש, bidders who back out, and appraisal by three
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about redeeming a consecrated ancestral field from הקדש. The owner must add a חומש on his own bid, but not on an outsider's raise, so at an outside bid of 26 he must pay 31 and a דינר or lose the field. The גמרא opens with רב חסדא. He says a bidder who backs out pays only the gap down to the next offer when that lower offer is still standing. If several bidders back out together, they share the loss, and a ברייתא confirms this split. Next, the גמרא explains why the owner's חומש gives him priority here but not with מעשר שני: here the חומש goes to הקדש. It then shows why the owner cannot claim a tie at 25, since he had added a tiny פרוטה. רב חסדא also limits the 'no חומש on the raise' rule to a field that three people did not appraise. The גמרא shows that this fits בית הלל. Finally, it explains that at 26 the owner is not forced to redeem, and רב ששת begins explaining the extra דינר, a point that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The owner's price climbs one סלע at a time with each outside bid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list. The owner bid 20, and for each higher outside bid from 21 to 25, the owner's price goes up by one סלע, from 26 to 30.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If the owner said 20 and another said 21,] the owner pays 26. If another said 22, the owner pays 27. If 23, the owner pays 28. If 24, the owner pays 29. If 25, the owner pays 30.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is running through a number chart. It shows what the owner must pay to keep his field when an outsider outbids him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner always pays his own bid of 20, plus a חומש of 5 on that bid. On top of that, he must match the outsider's extra amount so הקדש does not lose. So each extra סלע the outsider bids adds exactly one סלע to the owner's price, not more.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner (literally 'owners'), the one who originally consecrated the field
A coin worth four דינרים; the unit used in these bids
Redemption: buying back something consecrated from הקדש

phrases.english: the owner gives twenty-six;
if another said "for twenty-two" —
the owner gives twenty-seven;
"for twenty-three" —
the owner gives twenty-eight;
"for twenty-four" —
the owner gives twenty-nine;
"for twenty-five" —
the owner gives thirty,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's case from the previous section, where the owner bid 20 and an outsider bid 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Owner's price = his bid (20) + his חומש (5) + the outsider's extra over 20. So outside bids of 21–25 mean the owner pays 26–30.

steps.title: Why the owner pays no extra fifth on the outsider's raise
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the reason behind its chart. The owner's חומש is figured only on his own bid, never on the amount the other person added.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we do not add a fifth onto this other person's increase.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the math from Step 1. The חומש is calculated on the owner's own bid and not on the outsider's raise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the owner should pay a fifth on the whole final price. The משנה says no: the חומש attaches only to the owner's own offer of 20. The outsider's extra amount is simply matched one-for-one.

keyTerms.meaning: An added fifth that an owner pays when redeeming his own consecrated item (a quarter of the base, which equals a fifth of the total)
An increase or raise in the bid

steps.confusionAlert: The 'fifth' is a fifth of the final total, which equals a quarter of the base bid. That is why a bid of 20 gets a חומש of 5, not 4.

phrases.english: for one does not add a fifth
onto the increase of this one.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the outside bidder. His extra amount gets no fifth added to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין מוֹסִיפִין חוֹמֶשׁ עַל עִלּוּיוֹ שֶׁל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the principle that explains the number chart in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner's חומש is figured only on his own bid, not on the outsider's added amount.

steps.title: When the outsider bids 26, the owner must pay 31 and a דינר or lose the field
steps.stepSummary: Once the outsider bids 26, he has passed the 25 the owner would pay with his חומש. The owner can keep the field for 31 and a דינר; if he won't pay that, the field goes to the bidder.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one person said, 'It is mine for twenty-six,' and the owner is willing to give thirty-one and a דינר, the owner comes first. If not, the treasurer says to the bidder, 'It has come to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה reaches the turning point. The outside bid is now higher than the owner's bid plus his חומש, so the owner's price jumps by an extra דינר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to 25, the outsider's bid never passed the owner's 20 + 5, so the owner just matched the difference. At 26 the outsider goes beyond that, and the owner's price becomes 31 and a דינר rather than simply 31. If the owner refuses, הקדש cannot force him, and the field is sold to the bidder.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth a quarter of a סלע
Have priority; come first
'It has reached you': the field is now yours

steps.whatToRemember: The owner gets first rights to his field, but only if he pays the full price the משנה sets. At 26, that price is 31 and a דינר; otherwise the outsider gets it.

phrases.english: If one said: "It is hereby mine for twenty-six,"
if the owner wished
to give thirty-one and a dinar —
the owner comes first;
and if not —
he says to him: "It has come to you."
phrases.notes: The Temple treasurer is speaking to the outside bidder, telling him the field is now his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֶחָד: הֲרֵי שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the chart from Step 1 to the point where the outside bid passes the owner's bid plus חומש, which changes the result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At an outside bid of 26, the owner keeps the field only by paying 31 and a דינר; otherwise it goes to the bidder.

steps.title: רב חסדא limits the case of the fifty-bidder who backs out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רב חסדא. He limits an earlier line in the משנה: we collect ten from the bidder of fifty who backed out only if the bidder of forty is still ready to buy.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב חסדא said: They only taught this when the one who bid forty is still standing in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by narrowing an earlier ruling of the משנה. That ruling was about a bidder of fifty who retracted and had ten סלעים taken from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if the bidder of fifty backs out, we take ten from him and sell to the bidder of forty. רב חסדא says this works only if the forty-bidder still wants the field, because then הקדש's loss is exactly ten. If the forty-bidder has also dropped out, the loss could be bigger, so the ruling as written does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They taught this only…': a phrase that limits a משנה to a specific situation
Still standing by his offer; still ready to buy
Backing out of an offer (the earlier case רב חסדא is discussing)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's 'take ten' rule is really about making up הקדש's actual loss. This sets up the discussion that follows about what happens when the next bidder is no longer available.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Chisda said:
They taught this only
where the one who bid forty stands in his place.
phrases.notes: He's pointing back to the earlier משנה case: the bidder of fifty backed out, and we collected ten from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶּן אַרְבָּעִים עוֹמֵד בִּמְקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא and returns to an earlier line of the משנה (the fifty-bidder who backed out), not to the number chart just above.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Collecting only ten from the retracting fifty-bidder applies only when the forty-bidder still stands ready to buy.

steps.title: If the forty-bidder also backs out, the loss is shared
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא completes his rule. If the forty-bidder is not ready to buy either, the fifty-bidder and the forty-bidder share the payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the one who bid forty does not stand by his bid, they divide the loss between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes the rule he began in Step 4. He tells us what happens when the forty-bidder also backs out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, the fifty-bidder pays the full ten only when the forty-bidder still wants the field. Here, the forty-bidder also backs out. Now the fifty-bidder does not carry the loss alone; the two of them share it.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands in his place, meaning he still stands by his bid
They divide the payment between them

steps.whyThisMatters: This sharing rule is what the גמרא is about to test against the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים עוֹמֵד בִּמְקוֹמוֹ,
phrases.english: But if the one who bid forty does not stand in his place,
phrases.notes: He means the forty-bidder also backed out of his offer.

phrases.english: they divide it between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵין בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים עוֹמֵד בִּמְקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's statement from Step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the lower bidder also backs out, the backing-out bidders share the loss.

steps.title: Why doesn't the fifty-bidder share when the forty-bidder backs out?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the forty-bidder backs out, we take up to ten from him. According to רב חסדא, the fifty-bidder should share that payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if the forty-bidder backed out, we take a pledge from him up to ten. Why? Let the fifty-bidder pay together with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from a line in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says the bidders share when more than one backs out. Yet the משנה puts the whole ten on the forty-bidder. So why doesn't the fifty-bidder pay part of it?

keyTerms.meaning: He backed out of his offer
We take a pledge (collect) from his property
Why?
Together with him

phrases.english: We learned: if the one of forty backed out,
we take a pledge from him up to ten.
Why? Let the fifty-bidder give together with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's sharing rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that bidders who back out share the loss
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes only the forty-bidder pay, with no sharing.

steps.title: There was no fifty-bidder
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a case where nobody bid fifty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where there is no fifty-bidder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in the משנה's case, no one ever bid fifty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no one bid fifty, there is nobody to share with. So the forty-bidder pays alone, and רב חסדא's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There is not

phrases.english: Where there is no one of fifty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's case includes a fifty-bidder.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's case has no fifty-bidder.

steps.title: Why doesn't the forty-bidder share when the thirty-bidder backs out?
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge comes from the משנה's line about the thirty-bidder.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the thirty-bidder backed out, we take a pledge from his property up to ten. Why? Let the forty-bidder pay together with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question on the next line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה again puts the whole ten on one bidder. According to רב חסדא, the forty-bidder should have shared it.

keyTerms.meaning: From his property

phrases.english: If the one of thirty backed out,
we take a pledge from his property up to ten.
Why? Let the one of forty give together with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge on the next line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The thirty-bidder pays alone, with no sharing.

steps.title: There was no forty-bidder
steps.stepSummary: Again the answer is that nobody bid forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where there is no forty-bidder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer: in this case, nobody bid higher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no forty-bidder, there is nobody to share with. So the thirty-bidder pays alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who bid forty

phrases.english: Where there is no one of forty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8
steps.terutzMaskana: No higher bidder exists in this case.

steps.title: Why doesn't the thirty-bidder share when the twenty-bidder backs out?
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge comes from the line about the twenty-bidder.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the twenty-bidder backed out, we take a pledge from his property up to ten. Why? Let the thirty-bidder pay together with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question a third time, now about the twenty-bidder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once more, the משנה makes only one person pay. According to רב חסדא, the next-higher bidder should share.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who bid twenty

phrases.english: If the one of twenty backed out,
we take a pledge from his property up to ten.
Why? Let the one of thirty give together with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge on the next line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The twenty-bidder pays alone, with no sharing.

steps.title: There was no thirty-bidder
steps.stepSummary: Again the answer is that nobody bid thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where there is no thirty-bidder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the same way a third time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no higher bidder, the twenty-bidder carries the cost alone. So far, this one answer has handled every line of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who bid thirty

phrases.english: Where there is no one of thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10
steps.terutzMaskana: No higher bidder exists in this case.

steps.title: The last line: the ten-bidder who backs out
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's last line says that if the ten-bidder backs out, we sell the field at its value and collect the rest from him. Why shouldn't the twenty-bidder share?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last part of the משנה: if the ten-bidder backed out, we sell the field at its value and collect the rest from the one of ten. Let the twenty-bidder pay together with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last line of the משנה and asks the same sharing question there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the field is sold at its real value, and the ten-bidder pays whatever is still missing. According to רב חסדא, the twenty-bidder should help pay. This step sets up a stronger challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The last part of the משנה
At its real value
We collect payment
The remainder, the amount still missing

phrases.english: If so, say the last part:
If the one of ten backed out,
we sell it at its value
and collect the remainder from the one of ten.
Let the one of twenty give together with him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the same challenge to the last line of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ten-bidder alone pays the remainder.

steps.title: The answer 'no twenty-bidder' doesn't fit the wording
steps.stepSummary: You can't answer that there was no twenty-bidder. If he were the only bidder, the משנה would simply say 'collect from him,' not 'from the one of ten.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too there is no twenty-bidder, then why does it say 'collect from the one of ten'? It should have said 'collect from him'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the usual answer by looking closely at the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling him 'the one of ten' suggests there were other bidders to tell him apart from. If he were the only bidder, 'from him' would be enough. So the answer 'there was no higher bidder' does not seem to work here.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
Here too
It should have said

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge comes from the משנה's wording, not from logic. The extra words 'of ten' show that other bidders were there.

phrases.english: And if you would say here too
that there is no one of twenty,
if so, why 'collect from the one of ten'?
It should have said 'collect from him'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי דְּלֵיכָּא בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects ahead of time to the answer that worked in Steps 7, 9, and 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The answer 'there is no higher bidder,' as applied to the last line
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'from the one of ten' suggests other bidders existed.

steps.title: רב חסדא: backing out together versus one after the other
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא settles the contradiction by saying the two sources speak of different situations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: There is no difficulty. Here, they backed out at the same time. There, they backed out one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: After the earlier answer was rejected, רב חסדא gives a new answer. When bidders back out together, they share the loss. When they back out one after another, the last one to back out pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source that says to divide the loss (the ברייתא, as the next step shows) speaks of bidders who backed out at the same moment, so no one is more to blame than the others. The משנה speaks of bidders who backed out one at a time. Each one who backed out while the next lower bid still stood caused a loss of exactly ten, and he paid that ten himself. So when the ten-bidder finally backs out, the remaining loss is his alone. The earlier answer, that there was no twenty-bidder, is no longer needed.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no difficulty; the two sources can both be right
At the same time, all at once
One after the other

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'here' (כָּאן) is not the משנה. 'Here' is the source that says to divide the loss, and 'there' is the משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said:
It is not difficult;
here, at the same time;
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the source that says the bidders divide the loss.

phrases.english: there, one after the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 13 rejected with a new way to resolve the challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two sources describe different situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the twenty-bidder also backed out, he should seemingly share the loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bidders share the loss only when they back out together. When they back out one at a time, each one pays the loss his own backing out caused, the drop down to the next bid that was still standing.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that bidders who back out together divide the loss. Since the משנה charges only one bidder, the two must be speaking of different cases, just as רב חסדא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: If all of them backed out together, they divide the loss among them. But we learned in the משנה that the treasurer takes collateral from his property up to ten. So must we not learn from this that the law follows רב חסדא? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says bidders who back out together share the loss. It shows that this fits רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the loss is divided when all of them back out 'together' (כְּאֶחָד). The משנה says the full loss is taken from one bidder's property. The only way both can be true is the split רב חסדא gave: together means divide, one after the other means one person pays. The גמרא agrees with the final 'learn from it.'

keyTerms.meaning: As one, together at the same moment
They divide it among themselves (literally, 'they split it into thirds')
They take collateral, meaning the treasurer collects from his property
Learn from this; a proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: Bidders who back out together share the loss. When they back out one after another, each one pays the loss his own backing out caused.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a baraita:
If all of them backed out together —
they divide it among themselves.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the loss to הקדש. The bidders who backed out share it among themselves.

phrases.english: But we learned in the mishna:
They take collateral from his property up to ten!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it as Rav Chisda said?
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רב חסדא's split in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's split between backing out together and backing out one after the other
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: if all of them backed out together, they divide the loss

steps.title: Second version: the ברייתא contradicts the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Some tell the discussion another way, as a direct clash between the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some raise this as a contradiction: We learned in the משנה that if the ten-bidder backed out, the treasurer sells the field at its value and collects the remainder from the ten-bidder. But a ברייתא teaches that they divide the loss among themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same discussion. Here the ברייתא is not a proof for רב חסדא. Instead it is the source of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the משנה, where only the ten-bidder pays, is set against the ברייתא, where everyone shares. The contradiction comes first, and רב חסדא's split answers it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Some people set these two sources against each other as a contradiction
At its real value
The remainder; the amount still missing

phrases.english: There are those who raise them as a contradiction:
We learned: If the one of ten backed out,
phrases.notes: 'The one of ten' is the person who bid ten.

phrases.english: they sell it at its value
and collect the remainder from the one of ten,
but isn't it taught in a baraita: They divide it among themselves!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the discussion from steps 12–15 in a different form, as a direct contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that only the ten-bidder pays
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the bidders who backed out share the loss, while the משנה makes one bidder pay all of it.

steps.title: רב חסדא's answer in the second version
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא gives the same split: the ברייתא is when they backed out together, the משנה is when they backed out one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: There is no difficulty. Here, they backed out at the same time. There, they backed out one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: In this second version, רב חסדא answers the contradiction with the same split as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law is the same in both versions. The only difference is how the discussion is set up. In the first version the ברייתא backs up רב חסדא. In the second version it is the question that his answer solves.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here... there': the usual way of matching each source to a different case

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is not difficult;
here — at the same time,
there — one after the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seem to disagree about who pays the loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of bidders who backed out together, and the משנה of bidders who backed out one at a time.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the owner and another person bid the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, where the owner's equal bid wins because he adds a חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If the owner says twenty and any other person says twenty, the owner comes first, because he adds a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next question. The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה that it is about to ask about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an owner redeems his own field from הקדש, he must add a חומש (a fifth). So an owner who bids twenty really pays more than an outsider who bids twenty, and that is why he comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner, the one who dedicated the field
An added fifth that an owner pays when he redeems his own dedicated item

phrases.english: If the owner says twenty
and any person says twenty, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: the owner comes first because he adds a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבְּעָלִים אוֹמְרִים בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְכׇל אָדָם בְּעֶשְׂרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the bids are equal, the owner comes first because of the חומש he adds.

steps.title: Challenge from מעשר שני: the base price matters more than the חומש
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about מעשר שני says that an outsider's higher base bid beats the owner's bid, even though the owner adds a חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean the חומש is preferred? But there is a contradiction: If the owner of מעשר שני says one סלע and another person says one סלע and one איסר, the one who said a סלע and an איסר comes first, because he adds to the base price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the owner's חומש really gives him priority. It points to the rule for redeeming מעשר שני, where it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מעשר שני, an owner who bids one סלע would really pay a סלע plus a חומש, which is more than a סלע and an איסר. Still, the outsider wins, because his base bid is higher. So there the base price counts and the חומש does not, which seems to go against our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Preferred; better
The owner (here, the owner of the מעשר שני produce)
A small coin, much less than a סלע
The base price, without the added fifth
Comes first; gets priority

phrases.english: Is this to say that the fifth is preferred?
But there is a contradiction:
If the owner says one sela,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת מעשר שני about redeeming מעשר שני produce.

phrases.english: and another says one sela and one issar —
the one of a sela and an issar comes first,
because he adds to the principal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the owner's חומש gives him priority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of מעשר שני, the outsider's higher base bid beats the owner's bid with its חומש. That suggests the חומש does not give priority.

steps.title: It depends on who gains from the חומש
steps.stepSummary: With הקדש, the חומש goes to הקדש, so it counts. With מעשר שני, the חומש stays with the owner, so only the base price matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, where the חומש is a gain for הקדש, the חומש is preferred. There, where the חומש is the owner's own gain, let the base price be redeemed for a proper amount; we do not care about the חומש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are different because of who receives the חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a הקדש auction, the owner's חומש goes to הקדש, so his bid really brings הקדש more money. With מעשר שני, all the redemption money stays with the owner, who spends it in ירושלים, so the חומש adds nothing. What matters there is that the produce is redeemed at a proper base price, so the higher base bid wins.

keyTerms.meaning: A gain, a profit
Property dedicated to the Temple; the Temple treasury
Let it be redeemed
Properly, fully
We do not care about it

steps.whatToRemember: A חומש gives priority only when the side being paid (here, הקדש) actually receives it. With מעשר שני, only the base price counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule is not a general 'the חומש wins' or 'the base price wins.' The question is who actually gains.

phrases.english: Here, where the fifth is a gain for the Temple —
the fifth is preferred;
there, where the fifth is a gain for the owner —
let the principal be redeemed properly;
the fifth, we do not care about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out a real difference between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חומש should count the same way in both cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חומש counts only when הקדש gains from it. With מעשר שני, the base price decides.

steps.title: Quoting the case of 25 versus 30
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if an outsider says 'the field is mine for 25', the owner pays 30.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if one person said, 'It is mine for 25,' the owner must give 30.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to set up a question about it. The owner had bid 20, an outsider bids 25, and the owner ends up paying 30.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner's 20 plus his חומש comes to 25. Now the owner must pay the outsider's 25 plus a חומש of 5 on his own 20, which makes 30. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is mine, meaning a bid to redeem the field
They (the owners) give or pay

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אֶחָד: הֲרֵי הוּא שֶׁלִּי כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: One person said: It is mine, etc.
For twenty-five, they give thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה after the מעשר שני discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When an outsider bids 25 against the owner's 20, the owner pays 30.

steps.title: Why can't the owner call it a tie?
steps.stepSummary: The owner's 20 plus חומש already equals 25. He should be able to say the outsider only matched him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the owners say: 'A man has come in my place.' His bid is just the same as mine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. The owner's bid with its חומש is 25, exactly the outsider's bid, so why is he forced to redeem it at all, instead of letting the outsider take it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 we learned that when the bids are equal, the owner wins because he adds a חומש. Here the two totals look equal (25 and 25), so the owner should be able to say the outsider has simply taken his place, and let him have the field at 25 instead of being forced to pay 30.

keyTerms.meaning: In my place, the same as me. The outsider merely matched the owner's offer.
The owners of the field

phrases.english: And let the owners say:
A man has come in my place!
phrases.notes: The owner means: this man offered exactly what I offered, so he didn't really outbid me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case quoted in step 21, using the rule from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the owner pays 30
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Owner's 20 plus חומש equals the outsider's 25. An equal bid should go to the owner, so he should not have to raise to 30.

steps.title: The owner's bid included a דינר
steps.stepSummary: The case is where a דינר was also part of the owner's bid, so the totals are not exactly equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the owners said a דינר as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the numbers were not a perfect tie. The owner's bid involved an extra דינר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there is a small extra amount, the two offers no longer match exactly. That means the owner cannot claim the outsider just matched him, and the משנה's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth a quarter of a סלע

phrases.english: Where the owners said a dinar as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bids were exactly 20 and 25, which makes a true tie.
steps.terutzMaskana: A דינר was also involved, so it is not a true tie.

steps.title: Then the משנה should mention the דינר
steps.stepSummary: If a דינר was part of the bid, why doesn't the משנה say so?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it teach 'a דינר'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the case has an extra דינר, the משנה should have written it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer that depends on a detail the משנה leaves out is weak. The גמרא asks why the משנה would hide a detail that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it teach, meaning let the משנה say so

phrases.english: Then let it teach 'a dinar'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the owner's bid included a דינר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה does not mention a דינר, so how can the case depend on one?

steps.title: The תנא wasn't exact about small sums
steps.stepSummary: The תנא did not bother to be exact and mention the small amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was not exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the author of the משנה simply rounded off and did not mention a small sum like a דינר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that the משנה uses round numbers and leaves out small change. That would explain why the דינר is not written.

keyTerms.meaning: He was not exact, meaning the תנא rounded off small amounts

phrases.english: He was not exact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should list every amount that matters.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה rounds off and leaves out small amounts like a דינר.

steps.title: But the משנה does mention a דינר elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: Later the משנה says '31 and a דינר', so it clearly is exact about a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is he really not exact? But the משנה teaches: 'If the owners wanted to give 31 and a דינר, the owners come first!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the תנא skips small amounts. The same משנה does write out 'and a דינר' in a later case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא bothers to mention a דינר in one case, he cannot be ignoring a דינר in this case. So the answer of step 25 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Come first, get priority

phrases.english: And is he not exact?
But it teaches:
If the owners wanted to give
thirty-one and a dinar,
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה's next case, where the outsider bid 26.

phrases.english: the owners come first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 25 using the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תנא is not exact about a דינר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה itself writes out 'and a דינר' in a later case, so it does care about a דינר.

steps.title: רבא: the extra amount was a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the owner added a פרוטה, an amount so tiny that the תנא did not mention it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is a case where the owners said a פרוטה, and the תנא was not exact.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer. The extra amount was a פרוטה, not a דינר, and the תנא would skip something that small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A דינר is big enough that the תנא writes it out, as step 26 showed. A פרוטה is the smallest coin, so it makes sense that it was left out. Even a פרוטה is enough to break the tie.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest coin, a tiny amount

steps.whatToRemember: The owner cannot claim a tie because a tiny extra amount, a פרוטה, was in the bidding. The משנה just didn't mention something that small.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Where the owners said a peruta as well,
and he was not exact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of steps 23 and 25 after the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) with a smaller amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra amount was a דינר, which the משנה would have mentioned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra amount was a פרוטה, too small for the משנה to mention.

steps.title: Quoting the rule: no חומש on the outsider's addition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the owner does not add a חומש on the extra amount the outsider bid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: because one does not add a חומש on his addition, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה to set up רב חסדא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner pays the outsider's full bid, but the חומש is only figured on the owner's own original bid. That is why it came to 30 and not more.

keyTerms.meaning: An added fifth. In practice it is a quarter of the base price, since a fifth of the total.
His addition, meaning the raise in price from the outsider's higher bid
Add

phrases.english: Because one does not add a fifth
on his addition, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה, after the tie question is settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner's חומש is not added on the outsider's extra bid.

steps.title: רב חסדא: only when the field was not appraised
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only if three appraisers did not value the field. If they did, the owner adds a חומש on the addition too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: They only taught this when the הקדש was not appraised by three. But if the הקדש was appraised by three, he does add.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא limits the משנה's rule. It holds only when no official appraisal by three people was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an appraisal, the outsider's higher bid is just his offer, so the owner's חומש stays tied to his own bid. If three appraisers confirm the field is worth the higher amount, that amount is the real value, so the חומש goes on it too.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of, a phrase that limits a rule
Was appraised, officially valued
By three people, an official appraisal

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an official appraisal changes the rule, because the higher price becomes the field's true value.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
They taught this only
where the consecrated property was not appraised by three,
but if the consecrated property was appraised by three,
they do add.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule quoted in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No חומש on the addition only applies without an appraisal by three. With such an appraisal, the חומש is added on the addition too.

steps.title: A ברייתא: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought in support. בית שמאי say a חומש is added on the addition, and בית הלל say it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way: בית שמאי say: they add. בית הלל say: they do not add.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב חסדא. The next steps show how it supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its face, the ברייתא is just a disagreement about adding a חומש on the addition. The support for רב חסדא only becomes clear once the גמרא asks what case the ברייתא is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not add (a חומש on the outsider's addition)

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Beit Shammai say: They add,
and Beit Hillel say: They do not add.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב חסדא's statement in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's point that appraisal by three is what matters
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל

steps.title: What case is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: If the field was not appraised, בית שמאי would have no reason to say a חומש is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it was not appraised, what is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what situation the ברייתא is about, and rules out the unappraised case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an appraisal, the higher price is just the outsider's offer, and there is no reason to add the owner's חומש on it. So בית שמאי's view would make no sense in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
What is the reason?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If it was not appraised,
what is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the ברייתא from step 30 to find the support.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ברייתא about an appraised field or an unappraised one?

steps.title: It must be an appraised field
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be about a field appraised by three, which matches רב חסדא's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where it was appraised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is about a field that was appraised. That is how it supports רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a חומש on the addition only becomes a real possibility once there is an appraisal by three. This shows that the appraisal is the key factor, just as רב חסדא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it must be

phrases.english: Rather, it is where it was appraised.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31 and finishes the support for רב חסדא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is about a field appraised by three, so appraisal is the key factor.

steps.title: Does רב חסדא follow בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב חסדא's rule matches only בית שמאי's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב חסדא ruled like בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 32 explained the ברייתא as talking about a field appraised by three people. The גמרא now notices a problem: in that case, only בית שמאי say a חומש is added, which seems to make רב חסדא follow בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that when three people appraised the field, the owner adds a חומש on the extra amount. In the reading from step 32, that is בית שמאי's view, and בית הלל disagree. The הלכה normally follows בית הלל, so it is a real problem if רב חסדא sides with בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggestion the גמרא usually wants to reject.

phrases.english: Shall we say that רב חסדא
said his rule like בית שמאי?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב חִסְדָּא דְּאָמַר כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what follows from the reading given in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule about a field appraised by three people.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא is about an appraised field, then only בית שמאי require a חומש on the extra amount. That makes רב חסדא match the opinion we normally do not follow.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about an unappraised field, and בית שמאי are being strict
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is really about a field that was not appraised. בית שמאי are strict even there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the ברייתא is about a field that was not appraised, and בית שמאי are being strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by going back on step 32. The ברייתא is talking about a field that was not appraised, and בית שמאי simply add a חומש even then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 asked why בית שמאי would add a חומש when there was no appraisal. The answer is that they are just strict. בית הלל do not add a חומש in that case, and that fits רב חסדא, who only adds it when there was an appraisal. So רב חסדא follows בית הלל, and his appraised case was never part of their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. The answer holds on to a reading the question tried to reject.
Was appraised, here by three appraisers.
They are strict.

steps.confusionAlert: This answer undoes the conclusion of step 32. The ברייתא is now about an unappraised field again, and בית שמאי's ruling is explained as extra strictness rather than as a sign that the field was appraised.

phrases.english: Really, it is a case where it was not appraised,
and בית שמאי are being strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33 by redefining the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes which case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about an appraised field, so רב חסדא matched בית שמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about an unappraised field. רב חסדא fits בית הלל, and בית שמאי are simply strict.

steps.title: Second answer: an appraised field, with the opinions swapped
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the field was appraised, but we switch the opinions so that בית שמאי say no חומש is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: really, the field was appraised, and reverse the opinions. בית שמאי say he does not add.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way out. It keeps the case as an appraised field but swaps who said what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the opinions swapped, בית הלל say a חומש is added on an appraised field, and that matches רב חסדא. The cost is that בית הלל end up the strict side and בית שמאי the lenient side. That is unusual, and the next step picks up on it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say. It introduces another answer.
Reverse, switching who holds which opinion.

phrases.english: If you want, say:
really, it was appraised, and reverse the opinions:
בית שמאי say: he does not add a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם דְּנִישּׁוֹם, וְאֵיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reverses the opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי require a חומש on an appraised field.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל require it, so רב חסדא follows בית הלל.

steps.title: Then it should be listed with the cases where בית שמאי are lenient
steps.stepSummary: If בית שמאי were the lenient side here, this case would have been listed with those rare cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then it should have been taught with the cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second answer. There is a known list of the unusual cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict, and this case is not on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swapping the opinions makes this one of those rare cases. If it really were one, it would appear on that list. Since it does not, the swap is unlikely to be correct.

keyTerms.term: קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
keyTerms.meaning: The collected list of cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict.
Then let it be taught there.

phrases.english: But then let it be taught together with

phrases.aramaic: קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל!
phrases.english: the leniencies of בית שמאי and the strictnesses of בית הלל!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיתְנְיַהּ גַּבֵּי קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer given in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The swapped reading of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A case where בית שמאי are lenient would be included in the list of such cases, and this one is missing from it.

steps.title: Back to the first answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on the first answer: the field was not appraised, and בית שמאי are strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really it is a case where the field was not appraised, and בית שמאי are being strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The second answer is dropped, and the גמרא returns to the answer from step 34.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about an unappraised field. בית שמאי add a חומש even there, and בית הלל do not. רב חסדא's rule, which requires a חומש only when the field was appraised, fits בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops one idea and goes with another.

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: in the ברייתא the field was not appraised. בית שמאי are strict and add a חומש, while בית הלל do not. רב חסדא follows בית הלל, and he adds a חומש only when three people appraised the field.

phrases.english: Rather, really it is a case where it was not appraised,
and בית שמאי are being strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the answer from step 35 because of step 36, and returns to step 34.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא is about an unappraised field where בית שמאי are strict, and רב חסדא follows בית הלל.

steps.title: The owner redeems only if he wants to
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה, the גמרא notes that the owner redeems the field only if he wishes to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if one person said, "It is mine for twenty-six," and so on. If the owners want to, yes. If they do not want to, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה, where an outsider bids twenty-six. It points out that the owner pays the higher amount only if he chooses to, and nobody forces him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the owner can pay thirty-one סלעים and a דינר and take back his field. The גמרא stresses that this is his choice and not an obligation. That raises the question of why he is not forced, and the next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on. The rest of the משנה's line is assumed.
They wanted to.
Yes.

phrases.english: If one person said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: "It is mine for twenty-six," and so on.
If they want to, yes, they redeem it;
if they do not want to, no, they are not forced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֶחָד: הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once an outsider bids twenty-six, the owner may redeem the field but is not required to.

steps.title: Someone else has come to take the owner's place
steps.stepSummary: The owner is not forced because he can say that someone else has come in his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owners can say: "A man has come in our place."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason the owner is not forced to redeem. The outsider's bid already covers the Temple more than the owner's offer did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner's twenty plus his fifth comes to twenty-five, and the outsider offered twenty-six. Since the Temple already gets more from the outsider, the owner can step back and let him buy it.

keyTerms.meaning: Gaps or openings. Here it means the place the owner left behind.

phrases.english: They can say:
"A man has come in our place."
phrases.notes: Literally "into the gaps": someone has stepped in to fill the owner's spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the owner is not forced, as noted in step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The outsider's bid already gives the Temple more than the owner's offer, so the owner can let him take his place.

steps.title: What is the extra dinar for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions an extra דינר on top of the thirty-one סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the דינר, what is its purpose?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the wording of the משנה and asks a short question about one detail: the extra דינר the owner pays. This question sets up רב ששת's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a strange-looking number: thirty-one סלעים plus one דינר. A דינר is a small coin, a quarter of a סלע. The גמרא wants to know what role this small extra amount plays in the case.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth a quarter of a סלע
What is its purpose? What is it doing here?

phrases.english: And the dinar, what is its purpose?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through the wording of the משנה, now moving on to the payment amount.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה adds one דינר to the thirty-one סלעים.

steps.title: רב ששת explains what the משנה means
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the משנה is talking about owners who wanted from the start to pay an amount reaching thirty-one סלעים and a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: This is what it is saying: If the owners wished from the outset to give a calculation that reaches thirty-one and a דינר...
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts answering the question by telling us how to read the משנה. The sentence is not finished here; his explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת uses the phrase הכי קאמר to show that the משנה must be read in a specific way. He says the case is where the owners wanted, right from the beginning, to pay a sum that adds up to thirty-one סלעים and a דינר. So the דינר is part of the full total the owners chose to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; a way of explaining how to read a text
The owners of the field
From the outset, from the beginning
A calculation, a total amount

steps.confusionAlert: The thought is not finished here. The next amud shows what רב ששת says happens in this case.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
This is what it is saying:
If the owners wished from the outset
to give a calculation that reaches
thirty-one and a dinar;
phrases.notes: Thirty-one סלעים plus one דינר. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question about the extra דינר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is talking about owners who wanted from the start to pay a total that reaches thirty-one סלעים and a דינר. The explanation continues on the next amud.
